products.name: Holistic AI
products.note: Bias auditing, risk management, compliance; strong technical depth; mid-market focus

reading.body:
Holistic AI addresses a gap between AI deployment speed and organizational visibility. The company builds tools to find every AI system in use across an organization, test them for safety and bias, and maintain compliance with multiple regulatory frameworks, positioning itself in a market where AI scaling outpaces governance infrastructure.

The platform's scope reflects a real problem in large enterprises: AI systems proliferate faster than IT teams can track them. Shadow AI, undocumented deployments, and fragmented ownership create risk that neither traditional software governance nor manual auditing can contain. Holistic AI's approach of automated discovery, continuous testing, and real-time monitoring for agentic systems addresses the operational side of this constraint. As organizations deploy more AI systems, governance tools become part of the cost structure for scaling safely.

This data does not reveal adoption rates, deployment timelines, or whether the platform materially affects how fast enterprises can actually build and deploy AI. It also does not cover whether governance tools themselves become a constraint on AI scaling, or whether they primarily reduce risk within existing deployment patterns. The company's stated focus on mid-market organizations suggests a gap between what enterprises need and what they can currently afford or implement at scale.

profile_text.body:
Holistic AI describes itself as an enterprise AI governance platform, offering what it calls one end-to-end tool to identify, protect, and enforce AI governance at scale. The company says enterprises deploy AI agents, models, and applications faster than their governance, risk, and compliance processes can keep up, and that those processes remain manual, fragmented, and spreadsheet-based. Its platform is presented as closing that gap by discovering every AI system in an organization, testing continuously for security and bias risks, and generating compliance evidence for security, legal, and board audiences.

Per its site, the platform scans cloud platforms, code repositories, and SaaS applications to build an AI inventory and surface shadow AI, classifying systems by risk level, owner, lifecycle stage, and business purpose. It lists AI red teaming with adversarial testing, jailbreak resistance, and prompt injection detection, plus more than 40 AI and ML test types covering performance, robustness, explainability, and safety. Built-in frameworks are named for the EU AI Act, NIST AI RMF, ISO 42001, and NYC Local Law 144, with automated control mapping and gap analysis, and the company describes a supervisory layer for agentic AI that observes behavior and intervenes when risk thresholds are crossed. The site cites Everest Group calling it a major contender in AI governance, CB Insights naming it among the 100 most promising AI companies, Avasant positioning it as a leader, and Forrester recognizing its AI governance capabilities. It also quotes customers at Unilever and MindBridge.

The company is listed in the AI governance and risk management platforms category, with bias auditing, risk management, and compliance noted, along with strong technical depth and a mid-market focus. No litigation is recorded.
